subject: Error: result would be too long a vector

messages.author: be649b4a2cbd3452
messages.subject: Error: result would be too long a vector
parts:
Hi Dr. Chalmers,

I have a dataset where I have randomly assigned a subset of items to each respondent, so each item has missing data, but roughly each item should have about the same amount of responses due to the random assignment. The dataset is quite large, with 60 items, and I am trying to estimate a 10- and 15-factor model. I use the following code:

cfa_15 <- mirt.model("One = 2-4
                    Two = 5-9
                    Three = 10-13
                    Four = 14-17
                    Five = 18-21
                    Six = 22-26
                    Seven = 27-30
                    Eight = 31-34
                    Nine = 35-37
                    Ten = 38-41
                    Eleven = 42-44
                    Twelve = 45-47
                    Thirteen = 48-51
                    Fourteen = 52-56
                    fifteen = 57-59")
                    COV = OnE*Two*Three*Four*Five*Six*Seven*Eight*Nine*Ten*Eleven*Twelve*Thirteen*Fourteen*fifteen")
Mod <- mirt(items, cfa_15, itemtype = "graded", SE = TRUE, TOL = 0.001, method = 'MHRM')

When I attempt to do this, I get the following error message and warnings:

Error in min(s, na.rm = TRUE):max(x, na.rm = TRUE) : result would be too long a vector In addition: Warning messages: 1: In min(s, na.rm = TRUE) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf 2: In max(x, na.rm = TRUE) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

The distributions for each item are attached for your reference. Thanks so much for helping me troubleshoot this error! 

Best,
Dina Dajani
